$comment: Illustrative machine-readable CBOM profile for PQC migration planning. DERIVED: this profile extends the interface disclosure baseline under the composition rules on the Profile page. It inherits every baseline rule, tightens one, and adds twelve per-interface rules and two product-level rules. Extension is monotonic, so a CBOM conforming to this profile also conforms to the baseline. The 'file' hint in 'extends' tells the validator where to resolve the base from; profileId and version are what a conformance claim cites.
title: PQC Migration Readiness (Example)

objective.$comment: C1. A derived profile states its own consumer and decision; it does not inherit the base's, because the whole reason to derive is that the decision differs.
objective.consumer: An operator planning a post-quantum migration across an estate of products it did not build.
objective.decision: For each interface a product exposes: whether it can be made quantum-safe, what enabling it requires, what enabling it costs in interoperability, and where the capability is not yet available, what is preventing it and who controls that.

appliesTo.$comment: Must lie within the base profile's range. A derived profile may narrow the accepted carrier versions and may not widen them.

overrides.note: Tightened from SHOULD/withholdable. Migration sequencing depends on knowing which library implements an interface, so a withheld value leaves the consumer unable to plan.

productRules.description: Product states how complete its declared interface set is
Product identifies at least one cryptographic provider

interfaceRules.note: Conditional. Applies only where the capability is enabled by a software update.
Whether the far end can be pinned or forced is sometimes contractual; a producer may decline to publish it.
Conditional. Applies wherever the capability is not already available.

exclusions.item: A date on which an interface will gain a capability
exclusions.reason: Interfaces do not gain capability independently of one another, and a date offered where the blocker is an unfinished standard is not one the vendor can keep. The profile records capabilityStatus, blockedBy and roadmapRef instead. See decision 0007.

exclusions.item: Any judgement as to whether an interface is quantum-safe
exclusions.reason: Inherited from the baseline. The profile requires the algorithm sets an interface uses and supports, and leaves the judgement to external versioned policy. See decision 0002.

exclusions.item: Internal migration plans, engineering schedules, and unreleased design detail
exclusions.reason: Outside the black-box boundary. Anything the profile requires must be declarable at an interface or stated as a property of the shipped product.

exclusions.item: Per-algorithm capability status within a single interface
exclusions.reason: Deferred rather than rejected. The worked example states status separately for key exchange and authentication, which the current rule shape does not express. Recorded as Q27.

changelog.summary: Initial draft. Derived from the interface disclosure baseline v0.2: adds product rules P3 and P4 and per-interface rules M1 to M12, and tightens inherited rule I9 to a non-withholdable MUST.
